item.title: The prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_{11}$- and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_n$-solvable groups, focusing on the cases $\mathcal{A}_{11}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$. These provide the first classifications of $T$-solvable groups for which $|\pi(T)|>4$. We develop structural and representation-theoretic tools for analyzing the possible prime graph complements and use them to obtain complete characterizations for both $\mathcal{A}_{11}$-solvable and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups. The methods introduced also provide a framework for studying analogous classification problems for larger alternating groups.
item.dc:creator: Logan Abounader, Austin Bell, April Beun, Elvis Cabrera, Dakota Nobuyuki Goto, Thomas Michael Keller

item.title: The Siemons--Wagner property and Bradley's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.24502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A transitive permutation group $G\le\Sym(\Pcal)$ is said to have the Siemons--Wagner property $\star_3$ if some three-point subset has a $G$-orbit longer than the orbit of every four-point subset containing it. In this paper we develop a structural theory of three-point orbits of finite $2$-transitive groups (orbit-length hierarchies, pointwise and setwise stabilizers, and their geometric realisations, including the unital and the ovoid), and we use it to completely settle Bradley's conjecture: a finite primitive group of degree at least $8$ satisfying $\star_3$ is isomorphic to $\PSL(2,7)$ or $\PGL(2,7)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhilin Zhang

item.title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
item.description: arXiv:2610.24836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.
item.dc:creator: Harjas Sandhu, Andreas Thom

item.title: An explicit section of the Laudenbach-type exact sequence of the big mapping class group of $M_\Gamma$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a locally finite graph $\Gamma$, Udall proved that the mapping class group of the doubled handlebody associated to $\Gamma$ is an extension of the mapping class group of $\Gamma$ by a possibly infinite direct product of $\mathbb{Z}_2$, and that this extension splits. We give a formula for Udall's section restricted to the pure mapping class group and, when $\Gamma$ has finitely many ends, on the whole mapping class group.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Andres Robinson Arrieta

item.title: On the strong domination relation of order sequences for some group extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a finite group $G$, its order sequence $os(G)$ is a sequence formed of the element orders of $G$ written in non-decreasing order. In [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025), no. 2, Paper No. 2.9], P. J. Cameron and H. K. Dey proved that if $G$ and $H$ are groups of coprime orders, $G$ is abelian and $K$ is any extension of $G$ by $H$, then there is a bijection $f$ from $G\times H$ to $K$ such that the order of $f(x)$ divides the order of $x$, for all $x\in G\times H$. In the same paper, the authors asked if the hypothesis ``$G$ is abelian" is necessary. We show that if this condition is dropped, the result does not hold in general.
item.dc:creator: Mihai-Silviu Lazorec

item.title: The locally quaternion group is a countable $B$-group
item.description: arXiv:2610.25022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A group $G$ is a $B$-group if every primitive permutation group containing a regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$ is doubly transitive. We prove that the locally quaternion group $\mathrm{Dic}(C_{2^\infty},c)$, the extension of the Pr\"ufer $2$-group by an element squaring to its involution and inverting it, is a $B$-group. This gives an example of a countably infinite $B$-group. This answers Problem 13.30 of the Kourovka Notebook. The proof analyses the automorphism group of an orbital Cayley graph through the central involution. In the main case two half-flip automorphisms generate, with their conjugates, an elementary abelian normal subgroup whose orbits form a nontrivial block system; in the remaining case, where the pointwise stabilizers of the two cosets of the Pr\"ufer group have order two, the conjugates of the central translation generate an elementary abelian normal subgroup, which would be regular if the automorphism group were primitive; an affine lemma for the Pr\"ufer group excludes this. The proof does not depend on computer verification: its two finite case analyses are written out in full, and programs that re-check them are provided as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: Lambda number of the reduced power graph of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reduced power graph $\Gamma_{RP}(G)$ of a group $G$ is a simple graph with vertex set $G$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $\langle u \rangle \subset \langle v \rangle$ or $\langle v \rangle \subset \langle u \rangle$. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of a graph $\Gamma$ is a mapping from the vertex set of $\Gamma$ to the set of non-negative integers such that the labels of adjacent vertices differ by at least $2$ and the labels of vertices at distance two are distinct. The lambda number of $\Gamma$, denoted by $\lambda(\Gamma)$, is defined as the minimum possible span of labels among all $L(2,1)$-labelings of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ and characterize the conditions under which these bounds are achieved. As an application, we determine the exact value of $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ for certain classes of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Malviy, Keerttiranjan Sahoo, Vipul Kakkar

item.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
item.description: arXiv:2610.25030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Caputi, Francesco G. Russo

item.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.
item.dc:creator: Eniola Kazeem (FUTA), Francesco G. Russo (UNICAM)

item.title: Model Theory and Algorithms for One-Relator Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the elementary theories and algorithmic properties of one-relator groups. We give a first-order sentence characterizing Baumslag-Solitar-freeness in this class. For fixed $|m|>1$, we regularly interpret $\BS(1,m)$ as a definable subgroup in every one-relator group containing it. We uniformly, regularly and injectively interpret integer arithmetic in countable groups of cohomological dimension at most two. We obtain one uniform interpretation for all one-relator groups containing a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. Every fixed finitely presented group is regularly interpretable in these groups, and their elementary theories are undecidable. We also describe the GBS overgroups of a non-unimodular Baumslag--Solitar subgroup. For the unimodular groups we construct finite-index direct products of free groups and $\Z$, and reduce the elementary theory of $\BS(k,k)$ to that of a free group with a named periodic automorphism. Using the recent Open AI result that BS-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic we obtain a terminating algorithm recognizing this class and obtain consequences. From the virtual compact specialness result of another Open AI paper, we obtain an effective construction of virtual free-by-cyclic presentations for hyperbolic one-relator groups, the free kernel may have infinite rank. For classes of torsion-free one-relator groups in which CSA implies toral relative hyperbolicity, we give a uniform algorithm deciding CSA and, in the affirmative case, the existence of a subgroup isomorphic to $\Z^2$.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharlampovich, Alexei Miasnikov

item.title: Thompson's groups are sofic
item.description: arXiv:2610.25415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Thompson's groups $F$, $T$ and $V$ are sofic. As a corollary, all of them are also hyperlinear and not permutation stable. The proof relies on an explicit construction of sofic approximations to $F$ and $V$. Moreover, the construction allows us to obtain effective quantitative bounds on the parameters of sofic approximations.
item.dc:creator: Maksym Chaudkhari, Kate Juschenko, Kyrylo Muliarchyk

item.title: On quandles with isomorphic enveloping groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a method to construct two injective connected finite quandles of different cardinal with isomorphic enveloping groups.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Maassarani

item.title: On Huppert's $\rho$-$\sigma$ conjecture for primes in the orders of elements
item.description: arXiv:2610.25571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho(G)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $|G|$, and let $\sigma(G)$ be the maximal number of distinct prime divisors of the order of an element of $G$. Let $\rho(n)=\max\{\rho(G) \mid G \text{ solvable}, \sigma(G)=n\}$. We prove that $\rho(n)\le 4n-1+\pi(2n)$ for all $n$, and, with the help of a computer, that $\rho(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\le 16$. In particular, $\rho(n)\le\lfloor 9n/2\rfloor+2$ and $\rho(n)\le (101/22)n$ for all $n$, and $\rho(n)\le 9n/2$ for all $n\ge 58$. This improves the bound $\rho(n)\le (17/3)n$ due to Yang, and it shows that the bound $\rho(n)\le 5n$ stated by Bellotti, Keller and Trudgian holds, although its original proof contains a gap. Moreover, we show that $\rho(n)\ge 3n$ for all $n\ge 4$, which proves one half of a conjecture of the second author stating that $\rho(n)=3n$ for $n\ge 4$. We also derive a consequence for character codegrees and, conditionally, for arbitrary finite groups. The proofs of the main results do not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Jabara, Thomas Michael Keller

item.title: Linear Group Actions with Exactly One Regular Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2610.25737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $G$ a finite $p$-group, and $V$ a finite faithful irreducible $G$-module. We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then $p=2^{n}-1$ is a Mersenne prime and $(G,V)$ embeds into $(P_m,V_m)$ for some $m\ge 1$, where $P_m$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the monomial group ${\rm GL}_1(2^{n})\wr S_{p^{m-1}}$ and $V_m$ is its natural module, regarded over ${\Bbb F}_2$. We determine the largest orbit size $p^{x_m}$ of $P_m$ on $V_m$ and the number of orbits of this size, and we construct subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ whose unique regular orbit is a largest orbit of $P_m$; for $p=3$ such subgroups exist for every $m$, whereas for Mersenne primes $p\ge 7$ we prove that they exist only for $m\ge 3$. Finally, we classify the subgroups of $P_m$ of order $p^{x_m}$ with exactly one regular orbit for $m=2$ and, with the help of a computer, for $p=3$ and $m=3$, where there are $13$ such pairs up to isomorphism; for $p=3$ and $m=4$ we show that there are exactly $4914$ conjugacy classes of such subgroups in $P_4$. In particular, such a subgroup is in general not determined by its regular orbit.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Michael Keller, Jeffrey M. Riedl

item.title: Property RD and boundary representations]{Property RD for $\widetilde A_2$ groups\\and boundary representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a boundary representation approach to Rapid Decay property for groups acting on buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$. The central estimate combines a multiplicity argument on the product of Furstenberg boundary with the Riesz--Thorin theorem. For simply transitive actions on vertices, we also establish the polynomial bound conjectured by Ramagge, Robertson and Steger in the vector-radial case. The cubic degree of this bound is optimal. The method also uses multiplicity argument with the Riesz--Thorin theorem but on the single Furstenberg boundary.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Boyer, Thang Nguyen

item.title: On the kissing number of hyperbolic surfaces with a small systole
item.description: arXiv:2610.24222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parlier proved that there exists a constant $U>0$ such that for any hyperbolic surface $S$ of genus $g$ with systole $\ell$ the following holds: \[ Kiss(S)\leq U \frac {e^\ell}\ell g \] where $Kiss(S)$ is the maximum number of homotopically distinct systoles in $S$ (Kissing number). We show that there exists a constant $V>0$ and a sequence $S_n$ of hyperbolic homogeneous surfaces of genus $g_n\to \infty$ with a bounded systole such that \[ Kiss(S_n)\geq Vg_n \] for all $n\geq 1$. This shows that Parlier's theorem is sharp for a fixed systole length. Our proof uses Bruhat--Tits buildings of type $\tilde A_2$ and Hamiltonian surfaces.
item.dc:creator: S. Barr\'e, M. Pichot

item.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory. The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.
item.dc:creator: Rufus Willett

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang

item.title: Bounded orbits on homogeneous spaces and bounded geodesics on locally symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a unified approach to proving the following two results: (i) Let $G$ be a Lie group, $\Gamma$ a lattice in $G$, $X=G/\Gamma$, and let $F$ be a one-parameter $\mathrm{Ad}$-diagonalizable subgroup of $G$. Then the set $$ \{x\in X:Fx\text{ is bounded in }X\} $$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $X$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 7.1]{AGK} of An-Guan-Kleinbock in 2015. (ii) Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center and without compact factors, $K\leq G$ a maximal compact subgroup, $\Gamma\leq G$ a torsion-free lattice, and $M=K\backslash G/\Gamma$. Then for any $p\in M$, the set $$\{\xi\in S_pM:\gamma(p,\xi)\text{ is bounded in }M\}$$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $S_pM$, where $\gamma(p,\xi)$ denotes the geodesic ray through the base point $p$ in the direction $\xi$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 1.2]{GW26} of Guan-Wu in 2026.
item.dc:creator: Chengyang Wu

item.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.26060v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.
item.dc:creator: Altyngul Naurazbekova, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.26288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2\nu_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2\nu_n(G)=0\), and \(\pi_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Mikhovich

item.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.26778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Cantrell, Pablo Carrasco, Emilio Corso, Federico Rodriguez Hertz

item.title: On the quasi-isometric classification of permutational wreath products
item.description: arXiv:2409.20159v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we initiate the study of the large-scale geometry of permutational wreath products of the form $F\wr_{H/N}H$, where $H$ is finitely presented and where $N$ is a normal subgroup of $H$ satisfying a certain assumption of non coarse separation. The main result is a complete classification of such permutational wreath products up to quasi-isometry, building up on previous works from Genevois and Tessera. For instance, we show that, for $d\ge k\ge 2$, $\mathbb{Z}_{n}\wr_{\mathbb{Z}^{k}} \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{m}\wr_{\mathbb{Z}^{k}}\mathbb{Z}^d$ are quasi-isometric if and only if $n$ and $m$ are powers of a common number. We also discuss biLipschitz equivalences between permutational wreath products, their scaling groups, as well as the quasi-isometric classification of other halo products built out of such permutational lamplighters.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Dumoncel

item.title: Presenting the Zassenhaus Lie algebra by the Magnus Lie algebra
item.description: arXiv:2511.13379v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that the Zassenhaus restricted $\mathbb F_p$-Lie algebra of a (pro-p) group G can be presented by the Magnus Lie algebra of G. For the class of (pro-p) groups for which the terms of the lower central series are torsion-free, the Zassenhaus restricted $\mathbb F_p$-Lie algebra can be explicitly computed from the Magnus Lie algebra. These results apply to orientable surface groups, right-angled Artin groups, pure braid groups, fundamental groups of supersolvable hyperplane arrangements and fundamental groups of strictly supersolvable toric arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Ettore Marmo, David Riley, Thomas Weigel

item.title: A zero-one law for the spectral gap property of pairs in SU(2)
item.description: arXiv:2603.17869v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $n \ge 2$, Gamburd, Jakobson, and Sarnak [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 1, 51-85 (1999)] conjectured that almost every $n$-tuple in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ has a spectral gap. Toward this conjecture, Fisher [Int. Math. Res. Not. (2006)] established a zero-one law for $n \ge 3$, but obtained only a partial result for $n=2$. In this paper, we prove that the zero-one law also holds for $n=2$. We also remark that a Baire categorical analogue of this result holds.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Pikhurko, Kohki Sakamoto

item.title: Acylindrical hyperbolicity of automorphism groups and property $R_\infty$ for generalized Higman groups
item.description: arXiv:2604.27526v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Higman groups $H_k$ ($k\ge 4$) and their generalizations studied by Martin and Horbez--Huang. We prove that the automorphism groups of the Horbez--Huang groups on at least five generators, as well as those of Martin's $4$-generated Higman-like groups, are acylindrically hyperbolic. It follows that the groups themselves are acylindrically hyperbolic, admit infinite-dimensional spaces of automorphism-invariant homogeneous quasimorphisms, have infinite $2$-generated simple characteristic quotients, and satisfy property $R_\infty$. We also prove, using Delzant's lemma, a general criterion ensuring that an individual automorphism has infinite Reidemeister number: if $G$ is a group, $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, the group $\Gamma_\varphi=\langle\operatorname{Inn}(G),\varphi\rangle$ acts by isometries on a Gromov-hyperbolic space, and the restricted action of $\operatorname{Inn}(G)$ has two independent loxodromic elements, then $R(\varphi)=\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Ignat Soroko, Nicolas Vaskou

item.title: On the class-breadth conjecture for $p$-groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.13423v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The class-breadth conjecture of Leedham-Green, Neumann and Wiegold states that the nilpotency class of any $p$-group is at most $b(G) + 1$, where $\displaystyle{b(G) = \max_{g\in G}\log_p[G:Z_G(g)]}$ denotes the breadth of a group $G$. While several counter-examples to this conjecture have been found for $p = 2$, it is still open in general for $p > 2$. This article is dedicated to the general case $p > 2$ of the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Skutin

item.title: Mazurov's question on fixed points of automorphisms of free Burnside groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.33941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether an automorphism $\alpha$ of prime order $m$ of the infinite free Burnside group $G=B(m,q)$ of prime period $q$ that cyclically permutes the free generators of $G$ must have a nontrivial fixed point. In this paper, we show that for $m\ge3$ the answer is negative for all sufficiently large prime periods $q$. Precisely, we prove that for any odd $m\ge3$, there exists $q_m>0$ such that for every prime period $q>q_m$, the automorphism of $B(m,q)$ of order $m$ that cyclically permutes its free generators is fixed-point-free.
item.dc:creator: V. S. Atabekyan

item.title: Watkins's conjecture holds for all infinite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.01049v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that at every infinite cardinality, every group which is neither abelian of exponent greater than two nor generalized dicyclic admits a graphical regular representation, settling the infinite-group part of Watkins's conjecture. We also determine the Cayley index of every infinite group: it is $1$, $2$, or $8$, according to its algebraic type, and in every case the index is attained by a connected Cayley graph. For every infinite group $G$ of cardinality $\kappa$, we construct $2^\kappa$ pairwise nonisomorphic Cayley graphs with exactly the unavoidable inverse-pair symmetries, diameter two, and $\kappa$ common neighbors at every distinct pair. The principal tool recovers a continuous ordinal hierarchy from an alternating adjacency baseline with bounded-degree errors: robust finite patterns identify the initial classes, successive twin quotients recover the layers, and their finite exception packets determine the translation action. The reconstruction applies without a group action and is stable under additional layerwise bounded-degree edits. Further results give closed Cantor-cube families with prescribed finite data in the regular cases, sharp cofinality-dependent graph properties, and optimal three-valued shortest-path metrics.
item.dc:creator: Alex J. Sutherland

item.title: From almost tight $p$-group enumeration to $2$-group domination among finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.14509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. The pioneering works of Higman (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) and Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965), with improvement by Newman and Seeley, establish that \[ \frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac{4}{9}m^2+\Omega(m)\leq \log_p f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^{5/2}). \] In the same paper in 1965, Sims speculated on improving the error term ($O(m^{8/3})$ at that time) in the upper bound. To show that $f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3+O(m^2)$ is now known as Sims' conjecture. Our first main result proves Sims' conjecture in a strong form as follows: \[ \log_p f(p^m)\leq \frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac{4}{9}m^2+O(m). \] Techniques developed to prove the above lead to progress on some well-known open questions in group enumeration in affirmative, including: (1) 2-group domination in finite group enumeration (Pyber, \emph{Eur. Congr. Math.}, 1996): Let $F(n)$ be the number of groups of order $\leq n$, and $F_2(n)$ be the number of $2$-groups of order $\leq n$. Then $$ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{F_2(n)}{F(n)} =1. $$ (2) A question attributed to Higman and Erd\H{o}s (see Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman, \emph{Cambridge Tracts in Maths.}, 2007) when $m$ is large enough: $$ \text{for } 1<n<2^m, f(n)<f(2^m). $$ Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalisation by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-\Omega(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bl\"aser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term.
item.dc:creator: Yinan Li, Youming Qiao

item.title: Two-element factors and finite bases for additively idempotent semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every additively idempotent semiring $S$ in the constant-free signature, $S$ is finitely based if and only if $S\times E$ is finitely based when $E=M_2$ or $T_2$. For each $E\in\{L_2,R_2,D_2,N_2\}$, both implications fail even for finite $S$: we give a finite finitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is nonfinitely based and a finite nonfinitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is finitely based.
item.dc:creator: Qirui Ma, Mengya Yue

item.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Putignano, Matteo Vannacci

item.title: Partial actions of inverse categories and their algebras
item.description: arXiv:2405.13212v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we introduce partial and global actions of inverse categories on posets in two variants, fibred actions and actions by symmetries. We study in detail actions of an inverse category $\mathcal{C}$ on specific subposets of the poset of finite subsets of $\mathcal{C}$, the Bernoulli actions. We show that to each fibred action of an inverse category on a poset there corresponds another inverse category, the semidirect product associated to the action. The Bernoulli actions give rise to the Szendrei expansions of $\mathcal{C}$, which define an endofunctor of the category of inverse categories. We extend the concept of ''enlargement'' from inverse semigroup theory to inverse categories, and we show that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their Cauchy completions are equivalent categories; in particular, some pairs corresponding to partial and global Bernoulli actions are enlargements. We conclude by studying convolution algebras of finite inverse categories and showing that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their convolution algebras are Morita equivalent. Furthermore, using Kan extensions we also analyze the infinite case.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo M. Alves, Willian G. G. Velasco

item.title: Sign-coherence and tropical sign pattern for rank $3$ real cluster-cyclic exchange matrices
item.description: arXiv:2509.07454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The sign-coherence about $c$-vectors was conjectured by Fomin-Zelevinsky and proved by Gross-Hacking-Keel-Kontsevich for integer skew-symmetrizable case. We prove this conjecture associated with $c$-vectors for rank 3 real cluster-cyclic skew-symmetrizable case. Simultaneously, we establish their self-contained recursion and monotonicity. Then, these $c$-vectors are proved to be roots of certain quadratic equations. Based on these results, we prove that the corresponding exchange graphs of $C$-pattern and $G$-pattern are $3$-regular trees. We also study the structure of tropical signs and equip the dihedral group $\mathrm{D}_6$ with a cluster realization via certain mutations.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Akagi, Zhichao Chen

item.title: Morita equivalent blocks with an endotrivial source that are not globally isotypic
item.description: arXiv:2608.31083v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(K,\mathcal{O},k)$ be a large enough $2$-modular system. We construct two nilpotent block algebras of finite groups which are isomorphic as $\mathcal{O}$-algebras and are Morita equivalent via a bimodule with an endotrivial source of $\mathcal{O}$-rank $3$, but which are not globally isotypic. Hence they are not $2$-permutation equivalent and not splendidly Rickard equivalent. These results separate Morita equivalences with endopermutation source from $p$-permutation equivalences and splendid Rickard equivalences, and also separate almost global isotypies from global isotypies.
item.dc:creator: Xin Huang

item.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15419v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.
item.dc:creator: F. V. Weinstein

item.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.10111v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{\k{a}}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Alexander D\k{a}browski

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: Applications of $C^*$-Entropy to Representation Growth for Discrete Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21080v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological $1$-bounded entropy $h^\text{top}(C^*(\Gamma))$ of the full group $C^*$-algebra of a finitely generated group $\Gamma$ is given a representation-theoretic interpretation. The implications of Hilbert-Schmidt stability and matricial stability are investigated within this setting, recovering and strengthening a representation growth result of Hadwin and Shulman. The entropy framework is used to prove upper bounds on representation growth for superrigid groups and property (T) groups. This recovers a result of De La Harpe, Robinson, and Valette on the growth rate of the irreducible unitary representations of a property (T) group within the framework of $1$-bounded entropy. A soft proof that $SL_n(\Z)$ admits subexponential representation growth is recorded.
item.dc:creator: Connor MacMahon
